title: Шеф остаётся, а Катя улетает  (The Chef Stays and Katya Flies Out)

segments.t: The kitchen crew rejoices when Chef Barinov announces he is staying to protect the restaurant he built, and Katya stops by the bar to say goodbye to Denis before her flight. Listen to the Russian scene.
Шеф, так вы остаётесь с нами?
Шеф сделал этот прекрасный ресторан.
Слава богу, сегодня нас пронесло!
Старый кредит отдам и новый возьму.
Дома хороший кондиционер поставлю.
Жене дома в шубе жарко.
За что она хотела меня уволить?
Просто я плохо вчера старался.
Ну всё, я еду в аэропорт.
Давай, пока, счастливого пути!
Люблю тебя. Не скучай.
Я очень буду скучать.
Мама, пока, до встречи!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Шеф, так вы остаётесь с нами?
'Chef, so you are staying with us?' The grammar packs 'Chef Barinov' and 'us' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Шеф сделал этот прекрасный ресторан.
'The chef built this wonderful restaurant.' The grammar packs 'Chef Barinov' and 'restaurant' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Слава богу, сегодня нас пронесло!
'Thank goodness, we dodged a bullet today!' Notice how Russian expresses 'glory' and 'trouble passed' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Старый кредит отдам и новый возьму.
'I will pay off the old loan and take a new one.' The grammar packs 'old' and 'will take' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Дома хороший кондиционер поставлю.
'I will install a good air conditioner at home.' The meaning hinges on 'at home' working together with 'will set' in spoken Russian.
Жене дома в шубе жарко.
'My wife is hot at home in her fur coat.' In Russian, the idea of 'wife' flows naturally into 'hot' without extra filler words. Denis answers right away.
За что она хотела меня уволить?
'Why did she want to fire me?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'for' before landing on 'to fire'.
Просто я плохо вчера старался.
'I just did not try hard enough yesterday.' Notice how Russian expresses 'simply' and 'tried hard' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Ну всё, я еду в аэропорт.
'Well, that is it, I am heading to the airport.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'airport'. Denis answers right away.
Давай, пока, счастливого пути!
'Alright, bye, have a safe trip!' Denis brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'for now' in a few short words.
Люблю тебя. Не скучай.
'I love you. Do not miss me too much.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'like' before landing on 'miss'.
Я очень буду скучать.
'I will miss you very much.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'to miss' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Katya answers right away.
Мама, пока, до встречи!
'Mom, bye, see you soon!' The meaning hinges on 'mom' working together with 'meeting' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

And that sends Katya off toward the airport while Senya plans his next loan. Notice the affectionate farewell 'Lyublyu tebya. Ne skuchay'. See you in the next scene.
Я буду ждать твоего возвращения!
